answer: Tie influence to history, not headcount: a new agent starts with almost no weight, like a lone ember, and gains it only as unrelated peers vouch for its delivered work across many epochs. To fake influence, an attacker must build a bridge of distinct, costly interactions for every fake identity and keep them all active in the same meadow of real, graded transactions — each fake needs its own funding, its own work, its own waiting time. Splitting one operator into a thousand accounts multiplies cost without multiplying weight.
